newsitem.title: CANADA: Shareholders okay Toronto Sun buyout.
newsitem.headline: Shareholders okay Toronto Sun buyout.

text.p: Shareholders gave the planned C$411 million ($300 million) management buyout of tabloid newspaper group Toronto Sun Publishing Corp. an overwhelming thumbs up on Tuesday.
Less than one percent of holders voted against the C$16 ($11.68) a share buyout, which is due to close Oct. 7 if an Ontario court approves the deal on Wednesday.
The management team won an auction that Rogers Communications Inc. held earlier this summer for its 63 percent holding in the company. The management group then bid for the rest of the shares.
Another party has the right to make a higher offer until the closing on Oct. 7.
The buyout returns Toronto Sun to its roots as a tightly held company.

But there may be rough waters ahead for the now debt-laden company, which owns tabloids in Toronto, Ottawa, Edmonton and Calgary, Alberta, along with 60.2 percent of the daily Financial Post business tabloid.

"In any new company, there are always tough decisions... when you have C$250 million ($183 million) of debt, you have to look at things a little differently than when you are debt-free," management team leader and former Toronto Sun chief executive Paul Godfrey told reporters after the meeting.
Godfrey did not rule out asset sales or staff cuts. Many analysts believe Toronto Sun's debt may require it to sell its stake in the Financial Post.
"I would consider every possibility...Everything is on the table but I am not going to get specific because that is unfair," Godfrey said. "We have not made any decisions yet."
He said that current plans are to keep the Sun group intact, despite the onerous debtload.

Published reports said last week that Canadian newspaper chain Southam Inc. was interested in Toronto Sun's holding in the Financial Post. But Toronto Sun chief financial officer Bruce Jackson said on Monday the management group had not received any bids for the paper and were interested in keeping it.
